skills.name: Privacy getting started
skills.description: Use when a new owner first sets up this privacy bot, adds a household member, or asks to start personal data removal from scratch.
skills.content:
---
name: Privacy getting started
description: >-
  Use when a new owner first sets up this privacy bot, adds a household member,
  or asks to start personal data removal from scratch.
---
# Privacy getting started

1. Explain briefly: this bot removes the owner (and any household members they add) from data-broker, people-search, and face-search sites. It never pays, never starts paid trials, never creates extra accounts, never sends messages beyond opt-out forms, and stays quiet when nothing has changed.
2. Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
   1. Legal name, middle name, and any aliases, nicknames, or maiden or former names.
   2. Current city and state.
   3. Past addresses (city and state at minimum, street if they're comfortable).
   4. Phone numbers, current and past. Ask whether the bot may ever enter a phone on a form that requires one (default: no, lookups only; ask per site).
   5. Email addresses, current and past, including work ones. Brokers like PeopleConnect only send verification codes to an email already on the record.
   6. DOB policy: may the bot enter the date of birth on opt-out forms? Some sites lock it permanently once entered. If no, the bot hands those fields to the owner.
   7. Verification email for new requests. Recommend a dedicated bot email inbox so verification links can be clicked automatically.
   8. Optional, face search: which face-search opt-outs (PimEyes, Lenso, FaceCheck, Clearview) have already been filed, with their request IDs, and will the owner supply a photo or do those steps themselves?
   9. Household: should anyone else be covered (spouse, partner, adult family at the same address)? Recommend yes for anyone at the same address, since brokers list residents and relatives together.
   10. Reporting: who should get results and human-step batches (the owner directly, or a chief-of-staff bot they name)?
3. For each household member, ask (through the owner, one at a time):
   1. Consent: does this person agree to be covered? Don't search for or submit anything for a person without their consent, relayed by the owner.
   2. Legal name, middle name, aliases, maiden and former names.
   3. Current and past cities and street addresses (often shared with the owner).
   4. Phones and emails, current and past.
   5. DOB policy for this person, and their birth year or age range for matching.
   6. Which verification inbox to use (the bot inbox by default, or a plus-address of it).
   7. Relatives to use as match evidence.
4. Save the answers as memories (contact details in the vault), one set per person (never in shared skills or templates).
5. Create the ledger (for example ledger.csv in the bot's workspace) with this header:
   person,site,category,url,status,submitted_date,verify_method,needs_human,exposed_fields,notes,next_check
   - person: a short label for each covered person (for example owner, spouse).
   - exposed_fields: what the listing showed, separated by semicolons (for example name;age;address;phone;email;relatives;past_addresses;photo;property).
   - Status values: not-found, blocked, submitted, confirmed, relisted, needs-human, needs-review, skip. Use blocked when a page couldn't be read (see broker-opt-out-playbooks). It is never the same as not-found.
   - Add one row per site per person from broker-opt-out-playbooks (core and tier 2). Seed any opt-outs already filed as submitted, with their IDs, instead of filing them again.
6. Run the first pass: for each person and site, search, apply match-before-remove, run the browser pass on blocked pages, submit the confirmed ones per broker-opt-out-playbooks, and update the ledger. Do each parent company or family once per person.
7. Send one human-steps-batch at the end of the pass, including the manual steps list below for any item not yet done.
8. Turn on the monthly recheck routine (it runs relist-recheck; the quarterly report runs inside it), set to a day and time the owner picks.
9. Summarize what was submitted and what's waiting on the owner.

## Manual steps list (free; each needs the person's own account or identity)
Offer these once, during setup, as part of the human-steps-batch. Track each in the ledger as a row per person (category manual, status needs-human until done, then confirmed). Recommend all of them.
1. Google "Results about you" (https://myactivity.google.com/results-about-you, or Google app, profile, Results about you): each person turns it on with their names (including maiden names), phones, addresses, and emails, and enables email alerts. Then they add a filter in their own mail that forwards those alert emails to the bot's verification inbox. On each recheck, the bot reads the forwarded alerts and lists each flagged result with its "Request to remove" step in the batch.
2. Google refresh outdated content (https://search.google.com/search-console/remove-outdated-content): after a broker removal is confirmed but the old page still shows in Google, the person pastes the URL there. The bot lists the URLs in the batch.
3. Masking, so new signups don't feed brokers again:
   - Email: DuckDuckGo Email Protection (free @duck.com aliases) or SimpleLogin's free tier.
   - Phone: Google Voice (a free number) for signups and forms.
   - Cards: Privacy.com's free personal plan (needs a bank link; the owner's call).
   The bot never creates these accounts. If the owner sets them up, record in memory which alias or number went where.
4. Google Street View blur: in Google Maps, open Street View of the home, choose "Report a problem", select the house, and submit a blur request. The blur is permanent.
5. Zillow / Redfin home photos: the owner claims the home on each site (free owner account) and hides or removes listing photos. Check Realtor.com and Trulia too.
6. Credit prescreen opt-out (https://www.optoutprescreen.com): free. It needs an SSN and DOB, so the person does it. Online opt-out lasts 5 years; the permanent version needs a mailed form. Recommend the 5-year online opt-out at minimum.
7. National Do Not Call Registry (https://www.donotcall.gov): free; the person registers their own numbers. Skip if already done.

skills.name: Match before remove
skills.description: Use before opting out any people-search or broker listing, to confirm it belongs to the user (or a covered household member) and not a stranger, and to tell a real not-found from a broken search.
skills.content:
---
name: Match before remove
description: >-
  Use before opting out any people-search or broker listing, to confirm it
  belongs to the user (or a covered household member) and not a stranger, and to
  tell a real not-found from a broken search.
---
# Match before remove

Removing a stranger's listing is the main failure mode. Missing a real listing is the second. When in doubt, don't remove it, and don't call it clear either. Mark it needs-review.

## Who you're matching
- Match each household member separately, using that person's own identifiers from memory. Ledger rows carry a person column, so record the match against the right person.
- Identifiers per person: legal name, aliases and nicknames, maiden and former names, middle name or initial, age or birth year, current and past cities, current and past street addresses, known relatives (including the other household members), phones, and emails (personal, work, and past).
- A listing under a maiden or former name with a matching city, address, or relative is a candidate. Don't dismiss it because the surname differs.

## How to search (don't stop at name plus current city)
1. Name plus state, then name plus each current and past city. Repeat for every alias and maiden name.
2. Reverse lookups wherever the site offers them: each phone, each email, and each current and past street address.
3. Look at the address page itself. It often lists residents under names you didn't search.

## Evidence
- Strong (any one is enough with a name or alias match): an exact match on one of the person's own phone numbers, email addresses, or a current or past street address. A strong match confirms the listing even if the city, middle initial, or age is off, because brokers merge and misfile records.
- Supporting: age or birth year within 2 years, a current or past city, known relatives, and middle name or initial.

## Decide
1. The name (or a known alias or maiden name) must match.
2. Name plus 1 strong match: confirmed. Proceed.
3. Name plus 2 or more supporting matches: confirmed. Proceed.
4. Name plus fewer than 2 supporting matches, or anything conflicting (wrong age, unknown relatives) with no strong match: ambiguous. Set status needs-review, note why, and ask the user. Never remove it.
5. A strong match plus conflicts (for example the person's own email on a record in another town with a different middle initial): confirmed, but note the conflict. Never skip a record that shows the person's own phone or email.
6. Same name in a city the person never lived in, with no strong match and no other matches: don't remove it. Note it in the ledger (a lookalike skip-list in memory helps on recheck), then skip it.
7. Ads for other brands on a page (for example, TruthFinder ads on USPhoneBook) aren't that site's records. Match them through their own parent site.

## Broken or inconclusive searches (not clear)
Only set not-found when a real results page loaded for the right query and nothing matched. Treat these as inconclusive (status blocked, or needs-review, and retry through the browser pass in broker-opt-out-playbooks):
- a 403, challenge page, timeout, parked domain, or redirect to the home page
- zero results for a common name in a city where many people share it
- results that are only unrelated names (for example, a single person with a different first and last name), which means the search terms or filter didn't apply
- results for the wrong city or state despite a city filter
- a page that loaded but shows no search results section at all
Record the query, result count, and why it was judged inconclusive.

## Record
Put which fields matched (strong and supporting) in the ledger notes, with the screenshot path if one was captured. Don't include data beyond what you need.

skills.name: Relist recheck
skills.description: Use on the monthly routine to recheck opt-out sites for relisted records, resubmit removals, and report only changes; also covers the quarterly report and removal links the owner sends in.
skills.content:
---
name: Relist recheck
description: >-
  Use on the monthly routine to recheck opt-out sites for relisted records,
  resubmit removals, and report only changes; also covers the quarterly report
  and removal links the owner sends in.
---
# Relist recheck

1. Read the ledger. Select rows with status submitted, confirmed, relisted, blocked, needs-review, or skip, plus any whose next_check is due. Do this for every person in the person column.
2. For each broker or people-search site, search for each person using their identifiers in memory, including reverse lookups by phone, email, and address, and apply match-before-remove.
   - If a page is blocked, run the browser pass from broker-opt-out-playbooks. Never set not-found or confirmed from a blocked, empty, or irrelevant page.
   - Face-search sites (PimEyes, Lenso, FaceCheck, Clearview) can't be searched by name. For those rows, only check the verification inbox and the decision status. Never upload a face photo without the owner.
3. Compare against the ledger:
   - A confirmed or submitted site shows the person again: set status relisted and resubmit using broker-opt-out-playbooks.
   - A submitted site no longer shows the person on a real results page: set status confirmed.
   - A blocked site that now loads: search it properly and set the real status.
   - A skip site is back online: re-evaluate it and opt out if the person is listed.
   - No change: just update next_check.
4. Check the verification inbox for pending emails and update their rows. Also read any forwarded Google "Results about you" alerts and add each flagged result to the batch (see privacy-getting-started, manual steps).
5. Set next_check about one month out for every row you touched.
6. Collect new human steps into one human-steps-batch.
7. Report only changes. If nothing changed, stay silent, except for the quarterly report below.

## Quarterly report
Run on the recheck in January, April, July, and October (or whenever the owner asks).
1. Write the report to the bot's workspace (for example privacy/reports/YYYY-QN.md) and send a short summary through the normal reporting channel. The quarterly report is sent even if nothing changed.
2. Totals per person:
   - sites checked
   - sites with the person's info (ever found)
   - removed (confirmed)
   - pending (submitted, relisted)
   - waiting on a human (needs-human, needs-review)
   - blocked (couldn't be read this quarter)
   - new exposures found this quarter
3. Per-site table, one row per site per person, with these columns: site, status, exposed data types (from exposed_fields), submitted date, confirmed date, and screenshot path.
4. Screenshots: link the results and confirmation screenshots captured during the quarter. Don't capture new ones just for the report.
5. Open items: the outstanding manual steps and the top 3 recommended next actions.
6. Keep personal details in the report to what's needed, and never paste full DOBs or ID numbers.

## Removal link intake
Use when the owner (or the bot's manager) sends a URL that shows someone's info. There's no cap on these.
1. Identify the person it's about and the site. If the site isn't in broker-opt-out-playbooks, find its opt-out, privacy, or "remove my info" link in the footer.
2. Load the page (use the browser pass if blocked) and run match-before-remove for that person. If the match is ambiguous, set needs-review and ask, with a recommendation.
3. If confirmed, file the removal through the site's own form. Anything needing a phone, ID, or unsolvable captcha goes into the human-steps-batch.
4. Add or update a ledger row (person, site, url, status, exposed_fields, notes with the source URL), and set next_check about one month out so the monthly recheck covers it.
5. If the site is new, suggest adding it to broker-opt-out-playbooks in the next report.
6. Reply with the outcome: filed, needs a human step, or not a match.

skills.name: Human steps batch
skills.description: Use at the end of an opt-out pass to send the user one batched list of steps a bot can't complete, plus any open manual steps.
skills.content:
---
name: Human steps batch
description: >-
  Use at the end of an opt-out pass to send the user one batched list of steps a
  bot can't complete, plus any open manual steps.
---
# Human steps batch

Send one batch per pass, not one per site. Collect the steps during the pass and send them once at the end.

1. During the pass, when a step needs a human (phone verification, an ID or SSN, a face photo, an unsolvable captcha, a page still blocked after the browser pass, a DOB the bot isn't allowed to enter, a needs-review match), set the ledger status to needs-human or needs-review, set needs_human=yes, and add the step to the batch.
2. At the end of the pass, send a single list. Each entry has:
   - Person (whose listing or account it is)
   - Site
   - Exact step (what to click or enter, in order)
   - Why a bot can't do it
   - Link (the direct opt-out URL)
   - Recommendation (do it, skip it, or the bot's advice)
3. Put the highest-impact items first (parent companies that cover several sites, then sites showing an address, phone, or DOB).
4. Then add a "Manual steps" section with any open item from the manual steps list in privacy-getting-started (Google Results about you and alert forwarding, Google outdated content refreshes, masking, Street View blur, Zillow and Redfin photos, credit prescreen opt-out), plus any Google "Results about you" alerts that need a removal tap. List an open manual step on the first batch and the quarterly report, not on every monthly batch.
5. If no human steps came up, don't send a batch.
6. When the user reports a step done, update the ledger.

skills.name: Broker opt-out playbooks
skills.description: Use when submitting, checking, or rechecking an opt-out on a data-broker, people-search, or face-search site; gives each site's removal URL, required fields, verification, turnaround and gotchas, plus the browser pass for blocked pages.
skills.content:
---
name: Broker opt-out playbooks
description: >-
  Use when submitting, checking, or rechecking an opt-out on a data-broker,
  people-search, or face-search site; gives each site's removal URL, required
  fields, verification, turnaround and gotchas, plus the browser pass for
  blocked pages.
---
# Broker opt-out playbooks

Rules for every site:
- Run match-before-remove before submitting anything. Never opt out a listing that hasn't been confirmed as the right person.
- Never pay, start a paid trial, or create an account beyond what the opt-out itself requires. Don't send any message beyond the opt-out form.
- Do each parent company or family once per person. Its one request covers its child sites, but still search each child site on recheck and log it.
- Log every result in the ledger, one row per site per person (person, status, submitted_date, verify_method, needs_human, notes, next_check).
- Anything that needs a phone, ID, SSN, face photo, or a captcha you can't solve goes into the human-steps-batch. Don't stop the pass for it.
- Turnaround marked "unknown" means it hasn't been confirmed. Record what actually happens in the ledger.
- URLs change often. If a listed URL 404s, find the site's current opt-out, privacy, or "remove my info" link in its footer, use that, and note the new URL in the ledger.
- Some verification links expire in about 15 minutes (PeopleConnect, CoreLogic/Cotality). Click those first when working the inbox.
- Person-specific details (names, addresses, emails, skip-lists of lookalike profiles) live in the bot's memory and ledger notes, never in this skill.

## Blocked page browser pass
Many sites block automated fetches (403, Cloudflare or hCaptcha challenge, connection refused, parked domain). A blocked fetch says nothing about whether the person is listed.

Network route: when the owner has routed this bot's browser through their home connection (egress settings), the box browser already goes out from a residential IP, but shell commands (curl, WebFetch) may not. Never test or report the route from the shell. If you need to check it, load an IP-check page in the browser. Browser blocks on a residential route mean the site spotted automation (speed, behavior), not the IP: slow down, space out searches, and don't hammer one site. Never use proxy or network tricks to get past a block.
1. If a fetch or curl returns 403, a challenge page, a timeout, a redirect to a home page or parked domain, or an empty or generic page, set the row to status blocked (not not-found) and note what blocked it.
2. Retry the site in the box browser: load the home page, use the site's own search box (name plus state, then name plus city, then phone, email and address searches per match-before-remove), and screenshot the results page.
3. Wait out a Cloudflare interstitial once. Try a visible captcha once.
4. Only set not-found when a real results page loaded for the right search and match-before-remove found no match. Record the search terms used and the result count in notes.
5. Never mark not-found or clear from a blocked, empty, irrelevant (for example, only unrelated names for a common-name search), or error page. That is inconclusive. Leave it blocked.
6. If the browser still can't get a usable result after one retry, set needs-human, add it to the human-steps-batch with the direct search URL and opt-out URL, and move on.
7. Save screenshots of results and confirmations in the bot's workspace (for example privacy/screenshots/YYYY-MM-DD/<site>-<person>.png) and put the path in notes. The quarterly report uses them.

## Parent companies (do once, covers several sites)
- PeopleConnect: covers Intelius, TruthFinder, Instant Checkmate, US Search, ZabaSearch and Addresses.com (confirm the last two on the suppression page). One suppression request handles them all.
- BeenVerified family: BeenVerified, PeopleLooker, PeopleSmart, NeighborWho, Ownerly, NumberGuru, ReversePhone and MugshotLook share one opt-out platform (/svc/optout/search/). An opt-out on one is commonly reported to cover all; verify each on recheck.
- Spokeo family: AnyWho and PeopleWin redirect their opt-out to Spokeo's. Opting out on Spokeo covers them; verify on recheck.
- TruePeopleSearch / FastPeopleSearch clone family: each clone runs its own removal form. Submit each separately.

## Spokeo
- URL: https://www.spokeo.com/optout
- Fields: the listing's profile URL and an email address.
- Verification: email link.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: search first and copy the exact profile URL. There are often several same-name profiles in different towns, so match each one. Captcha. Also covers AnyWho and PeopleWin.

## Whitepages
- URL: https://www.whitepages.com/suppression-requests
- Fields: the listing URL and a phone number.
- Verification: an automated phone call gives a code. This needs a human, so it goes in the batch.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: automated listing searches are often blocked (403), so use the browser pass. A search that returns only unrelated names is inconclusive, not clear. Also check premium.whitepages.com and 411.com, which show Whitepages data.

## BeenVerified
- URL: https://www.beenverified.com/svc/optout/search/ (older /app/optout/search may redirect)
- Fields: name, state, street address and age. Don't guess the address or age. If they aren't in memory, mark needs-human.
- Verification: email link.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: captcha. Often blocks automated fetches (403). An FCRA "I agree" gate sits in front of the search; accepting it is part of the opt-out flow, not an account.

## PeopleConnect (Intelius, TruthFinder, Instant Checkmate, US Search)
- URL: https://suppression.peopleconnect.us/login
- Fields: email, then the record match details including date of birth.
- Verification: an email link that expires in about 15 minutes. Have the inbox ready and click the link right away.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: the DOB is permanent once saved and can't be changed, so follow the user's DOB policy. Each account is locked to one DOB, so a second household member needs a separate inbox address (a plus-address works). If the bot isn't allowed to enter it, hand the screen to the user for that field. Codes go only to an email already on the record, which may not be the bot inbox; ask the owner which email to use and note it. One request covers all brands.

## PeopleFinders
- URL: https://www.peoplefinders.com/opt-out
- Fields: name, location and email. Select the matching record.
- Verification: email link.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: captcha. Automated fetches are often blocked (403).

## TruePeopleSearch
- URL: https://www.truepeoplesearch.com/removal
- Fields: email, then select the matching record.
- Verification: email link plus hCaptcha.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: Cloudflare challenge. If the hCaptcha can't be solved, put it in the batch.

## FastPeopleSearch
- URL: https://www.fastpeoplesearch.com/removal
- Fields: email, then select the matching record.
- Verification: email link.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: captcha. Shares data with similar sites, so check each one separately.

## Radaris
- URL: https://radaris.com/control/privacy
- Status: skip. The site was seized under a court order (Atlas Data Privacy v. Radaris). Mark it skip and check whether it's back on each monthly recheck.
- Verification: when it was operating, email/account.
- Turnaround: unknown.

## MyLife
- URL: https://www.mylife.com/privacyrequest (old /ccpa/index.pubview returns 404)
- Fields: request type (Delete / Do Not Sell), profile URL if found, name, location, email.
- Verification: email code or link to the bot inbox.
- Turnaround: about 15 days stated; confirm on recheck.
- Gotchas: Cloudflare often blocks automated fetches. privacy@mylife.com hard-bounces (554 address not found), so don't use it. If the form fails, fallback email is membersupport@mylife.com (outbound send needs owner approval). Support may report "no records found" for the exact details; it offers a second review with name variations, other cities, or a profile URL, so find the profile URL first.

## Nuwber
- URL: https://nuwber.com/removal/link
- Fields: the listing URL and an email address.
- Verification: email link.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: often refuses the connection or won't load. Log it as blocked, retry in the browser pass, and don't count it as not-found.

## ThatsThem
- URL: https://thatsthem.com/optout
- Fields: name, address, phone and email from the listing.
- Verification: captcha; confirmation can take about 72 hours.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: captcha. Same-name records in other towns are common, so match carefully, but a record showing the person's own email or phone is a strong match even in another town (see match-before-remove). Entering a phone needs the owner's OK.

## USPhoneBook
- URL: https://www.usphonebook.com/opt-out
- Fields: select the matching record.
- Verification: captcha.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: its pages carry TruthFinder and Instant Checkmate ads. Those ads aren't USPhoneBook records. Handle them through PeopleConnect.

## Acxiom
- URL: https://www.acxiom.com/optout/ (old isapps optout.aspx redirects here)
- Fields: name, address and email.
- Verification: email link; the confirmation gives a reference number and about a 2-week timeline.
- Turnaround: about 2 weeks for opt-out.
- Gotchas: the landing page is informational; follow its link to the live consumer request form. The online form covers opt-out; a full delete may require a phone call, which goes in the batch.

## LexisNexis
- URL: https://consumer.risk.lexisnexis.com/opt (old optout.lexisnexis.com redirects here)
- Fields: name and address. May ask for SSN or other identifiers.
- Verification: email.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: never enter an SSN or ID number. Put it in the batch for the user.

## PimEyes (face search)
- URL: https://pimeyes.com/en/opt-out-request-form
- Fields: a face photo and an email address.
- Verification: a decision email.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: needs a photo of the user, so it's a human step unless the user supplies one.

## Lenso (face search)
- URL: https://lenso.ai/en/opt-out
- Fields: a face photo and an email address.
- Verification: a decision email.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: needs a photo.

## FaceCheck (face search)
- URL: verify the current opt-out page on the site before using it.
- Fields: a face photo.
- Verification: captcha.
- Turnaround: unknown.
- Gotchas: the captcha often defeats automation, so it's usually a human step.

## Clearview AI (face search)
- URL: https://www.clearview.ai/privacy-and-requests
- Fields: a face photo and an email address.
- Verification: a confirmation with a request ID. Save the ID in memory and the ledger.
- Turnaround: about 45 days, as stated at submission.
- Gotchas: needs a photo.

# Tier 2 sites
These are the remaining sites on the major removal services' standard lists. "Loads" means it returned the page when checked, "blocked" means it exists but refuses automated fetches (use the browser pass), and "find on site" means the guessed path 404s, so locate the current link in the site footer. Unless a site says otherwise, the method is: search the site, match-before-remove, copy the record URL, submit the removal form with the bot inbox, and click the email link.

## TruePeopleSearch / FastPeopleSearch clones (file each separately)
- FastBackgroundCheck: https://www.fastbackgroundcheck.com/opt-out (blocked). Select record, email link.
- AdvancedBackgroundChecks: find on site (footer "Remove my info"). Select record, email link.
- CyberBackgroundChecks: https://www.cyberbackgroundchecks.com/removal (blocked). Select record, email link.
- SmartBackgroundChecks: https://www.smartbackgroundchecks.com/remove (loads). Select record, email link.
- PeopleSearchNow: https://www.peoplesearchnow.com/opt-out (blocked). Select record, email link.
- USA-People-Search: https://www.usa-people-search.com/removal (loads). Select record, email link.
- FindPeopleSearch: https://www.findpeoplesearch.com/optout (loads). Select record, email link.
- Gotchas: same data and same captcha style across the family. A removal on one does not remove the others. These rank high on Google, so do them first.

## BeenVerified family (one platform, /svc/optout/search/)
- PeopleLooker: https://www.peoplelooker.com/svc/optout/search/ (blocked)
- PeopleSmart: https://www.peoplesmart.com/svc/optout/search/ (blocked; /help/ has the link)
- NeighborWho: https://www.neighborwho.com/svc/optout/search/ (blocked)
- Ownerly: https://www.ownerly.com/svc/optout/search/ (blocked). Property-focused; search by address.
- NumberGuru: https://www.numberguru.com/svc/optout/search/ (blocked). Search by phone.
- ReversePhone: https://www.reversephone.com/svc/optout/search/ (blocked). Search by phone.
- MugshotLook: https://www.mugshotlook.com/svc/optout/search/ (loads). Only if a record exists.
- KidsLiveSafe: find on site. Only relevant if it shows the person.
- Method: same as BeenVerified (name and state search, select record, email link). File on BeenVerified first, then confirm each sibling on recheck. If a sibling still shows the record, file there too.

## PeopleFinders family
- PrivateEye: https://privateeye.com/removal (loads). Select record, email.
- PublicRecordsNow: https://publicrecordsnow.com/optout (loads). Select record, email.
- PeopleSearch.com: find on site.
- Method: search, select record, submit. Treat each as separate until a recheck proves one form covers the others.

## Free people-search sites (each separate)
- SearchPeopleFree: https://www.searchpeoplefree.com/opt-out (loads). Record URL plus email link.
- ClustrMaps: https://clustrmaps.com/bl/opt-out (often times out; browser pass). Record URL plus email or captcha.
- Neighbor.report: https://neighbor.report/remove (often times out; browser pass). Record URL plus captcha.
- OfficialUSA: https://www.officialusa.com/opt-out/ (often times out; browser pass). Record URL, email.
- PeopleSearcher: https://www.peoplesearcher.com/optout (loads). Shows "Removal confirmed" after the email link.
- FreePeopleDirectory: https://www.freepeopledirectory.com/optout (loads).
- PeopleByName: https://www.peoplebyname.com/remove.php (blocked).
- USATrace: https://www.usatrace.com/optout (loads).
- QuickPeopleTrace: https://www.quickpeopletrace.com/optout (loads).
- DOBSearch: find on site. Shows date of birth, so it's high value.
- TruthViewer: https://www.truthviewer.com/optout (loads).
- CheckPeople: https://checkpeople.com/opt-out (loads). Select record, email link. The form sometimes sticks at the email step; log blocked and retry later.
- FamilyTreeNow: https://www.familytreenow.com/optout (Cloudflare; browser pass). Find the record, paste its URL, captcha, email link. Also lists relatives, so search maiden names.
- PeekYou: https://www.peekyou.com/about/contact/optout (loads). Profile URL plus email.
- OpenDataUSA: the domain sometimes redirects to a parked page. Use the browser pass; if a record page loads, use its "remove" or contact link. If the site is parked, mark blocked with the record URL from search results and recheck monthly. Don't mark it not-found just because the domain is parked.

## Voter data
- VoterRecords: https://voterrecords.com (blocked; browser pass). Each record page has a record opt-out or removal link. It shows address, party and age or DOB from public voter files.
- Gotchas: removal from the site doesn't change the official voter file. State voter-file confidentiality programs are out of scope; note them for the owner only if asked.

## Phone and directory lookups
- 411.com: Whitepages data. Handle through the Whitepages suppression flow.
- AnyWho: its opt-out redirects to Spokeo's. Handle through Spokeo.
- SpyDialer: https://www.spydialer.com/consumers/ (loads). Follow the consumer opt-out link; search by phone.
- ReversePhone: BeenVerified family (above).
- UnitedStatesPhonebook, AmericaPhonebook, FreePhoneTracer, CellRevealer, PhoneOwner.us: search by phone, then find the opt-out in the footer.
- Yellowbook / DexKnows: business directories. Act only if a home listing appears.

## PeopleWhiz cluster (likely one opt-out)
- Domains: peoplewhiz.com, peoplewhized.com, peoplewhizr.net, peopleswhizr.com, peoplewiz.com, peoplewizard.net, peoplewizr.com, people-wizard.com, peopleswizard.com.
- URL: https://www.peoplewhiz.com/remove-my-info (blocked; browser pass).
- Method: name and state search, select record, email link. On recheck, spot-check 2 or 3 clones; if any still show the record, file on that domain's own footer link.

## Background-check sites (search, then footer opt-out)
- SpyFly: https://www.spyfly.com/help-center/remove-my-public-record (blocked). Several of the sites below run on the same engine and accept the same style of removal request.
- BackgroundChecks.org, BackgroundChecks.me, BackgroundCheckers.net, CheckSecrets, PrivateRecords.net, PrivateReports, PublicDataCheck, TruthRecord, SealedRecords, SearchPublicRecords, SecretInfo, IdentityPI, Selfie.systems, PersonSearchers, PeopleSearchExpert, PeopleSearch123, PublicSearcher, PublicInfoServices, PublicRecordReports, Open-Public-Records, OhioResidentDatabase, FloridaResidentsDirectory, Weinform, InmatesSearcher.
- Method: most are funnel pages for paid reports. Search by name and state. If no free record page exists for the person, note "funnel only, no record shown" and set not-found only after a real results page loads. If a record exists, use the footer "opt out" or "do not sell" link.
- Many state-specific sites (Florida, Ohio, California) only matter if the person lived there.

## Marketing data brokers (no public profile; file a request anyway)
- Epsilon: https://legal.epsilon.com/dsr (loads). Consumer rights request: file both delete and do-not-sell, each with email verification and its own request ID.
- CoreLogic / Cotality: consumer privacy request portal; identity verification by email link that expires in about 15 minutes.
- Equifax marketing lists: free online opt-out; about 15 days.
- Experian: https://consumerprivacy.experian.com/ (state-based privacy portal). Pick the state, then opt out of sale/sharing, limit use of sensitive information, and opt out of targeted advertising. It requires a phone number (owner's OK needed) but not an SSN (leave it blank). No code was sent when tested. Gives a case number; acts within 15 days and completes within 45. It links a separate Tapad device opt-out; leave that alone unless the owner asks.
- Never enter an SSN; anything that needs one goes into the batch.

routines.name: Monthly data-removal recheck
routines.description: Fires once a month to catch relisted records, resubmit removals, and send one batch of steps only a human can do.
routines.content:
Follow the relist-recheck skill for every person in the privacy ledger (for example privacy/ledger.csv in the bot's workspace). Load broker-opt-out-playbooks, match-before-remove and human-steps-batch as that skill says.

- **Sites:** recheck every data-broker and people-search site, including reverse lookups by phone, email and address. For face-search sites (PimEyes, Lenso, Clearview, FaceCheck), check only the decision emails and status.
- **Blocked pages:** run the browser pass in the box browser on every blocked row and save screenshots under privacy/screenshots/<date>/. Never mark a blocked, empty or irrelevant page as not-found.
- **Resubmitting:** resubmit opt-outs wherever someone has reappeared. Use the bot's verification inbox (a plus-address per household member is fine) wherever an email is needed.
- **Inbox:** check the verification inbox for verification and decision emails, and for any forwarded Google "Results about you" alerts. Add each flagged result to the batch.
- **Ledger:** update statuses and dates, and set next_check about a month out.
- **Rules:** never pay, never enter an SSN or ID, never enter a phone number unless the owner approved it for that site, never create extra accounts. Any outbound email other than an opt-out form needs the owner's OK.
- **Quarterly report:** in January, April, July and October, also write the quarterly report to privacy/reports/YYYY-QN.md in the relist-recheck format and always send the owner a short summary.
- **Reporting:** send the owner the changes and one combined human-steps batch, with a recommendation on each item. In a non-quarterly month, if nothing changed and nothing needs a human, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Denver 28 9 15 * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
